entries.name: House mouse
behaviour: commensal with people in granaries, stables, houses and ships
females may breed within a month of birth
nests of shredded paper and cloth under floors and in walls
entries.notes: The uninvited tenant of every Mediterranean granary; a staple prey of barn, tawny and little owls.

entries.name: Black rat
entries.migrates: follows ships: ports and cargo are its highways
behaviour: sleeker and more agile than the brown rat; tail longer than the body
climbs ropes, cargo nets and olive trees with ease
carries fleas that spread plague; Marseille 1720 and Messina 1347 both arrived by ship

voxel_model.pattern: usually blackish; grey and agouti forms occur

entries.notes: The ship rat that followed Rome's roads and fleets; in port towns it is as much seafarer as rodent.

entries.name: Brown rat
behaviour: bigger, heavier and meaner than the black rat; tail shorter than the body
burrows along sewers, riverbanks and farmyards
displaces black rats where it settles; swims well

voxel_model.pattern: brown above, pale belly, naked pink ears and feet

entries.notes: The sewer rat; wrongly called Norwegicus after an English naturalist misread its northern origin.

entries.name: Greater white-toothed shrew
behaviour: fast, darting forager of stone walls and hedgerows
must eat every few hours or starve, like all shrews
chirps and clicks constantly while hunting

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, pale below, white-tipped flanks fade white in winter coat

entries.notes: A blur of legs and teeth in every garden edge; one of the commonest small mammals of French and Iberian villages.

entries.name: Etruscan shrew
behaviour: world's smallest mammal by mass; a paperclip of a hunter
heart rate up to 1500 beats per minute; must hunt constantly
may enter torpor in cold; finds shelter in stone walls and orchards
entries.notes: The shrew from Etruscan ruins; at 1.8 g it hunts prey nearly its own size to keep its paperclip metabolism fed.

entries.name: Iberian mole
behaviour: digging spade forelimbs thrown up like a swimmer's
builds the criss-crossing that network of ridges in meadows
nearly blind: eyes under skin, detects earthworm vibrations
entries.notes: The gardener's eternal riddle; the one mammal you meet only as a molehill and a missing worm.

entries.name: Edible dormouse
behaviour: hibernator: up to half the year in a tree hollow in deep sleep
fat as a pudding by October; Romans fattened them in clay dolia for honeyed tables
bushy tail, big black eyes, silent climber

voxel_model.pattern: silvery-grey back, cream belly, darker eye ring

entries.notes: Rome's glirarium fattened these for the feast of Caesars; a luxury slow food that is mostly sleep.

entries.name: Garden dormouse
behaviour: masked face and white-tipped black tail tassel
the most carnivorous dormouse; may take small birds and reptiles
brilliantly fluoresces hot pink under UV light

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, white tassel tail tip, bold black eye mask

entries.notes: Near Threatened and vanishing across its range; in the Mediterranean its island subspecies are critically rare.

entries.name: Greater horseshoe bat
entries.migrates: sedentary: 20 to 30 km between summer and winter roosts
behaviour: roosts in caves, ruins, mines and attics in dense clusters
echolocates at 81 kHz; cruises low and fluttering over cattle pasture
females faithful to birth roost; mating in autumn, sperm stored until spring
entries.notes: The cathedral organist of the cave behind the village; its whitewashed nose is a horn, not a smile.

entries.name: Common pipistrelle
entries.migrates: partial: northern colonies drift south in autumn
behaviour: the first bat flickering around streetlights at sunset
one of the smallest bats; smaller than a sparrow
feeds around houses and cattle; maternity colonies in roof spaces
entries.notes: Europe's commonest bat; dusk's first callers above the olive terraces.

entries.name: Barbary ground squirrel
entries.migrates: may move when argan crop fails
behaviour: colonies sunning upright beside burrows like tiny sentries
feeds morning and evening; retreats to burrow in midday heat
the argan tree's only disperser; introduced to Fuerteventura in 1965

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with a pale dorsal stripe and white flank line

entries.notes: The sentinel of the argan groves; Morocco's one wild squirrel, wise to your camera.

entries.name: Eurasian nightingale
entries.migrates: winters in sub-Saharan Africa; arrives late April, sings all night
behaviour: the sound of Mediterranean spring nights; up to 200 song types from one throat
plump rust-brown back, white breast, white-flanked tail cocked upward
sings insistently from April into June; a poet's bird since Ovid

voxel_model.pattern: warm chestnut above, pale belly, rusty tail cocked high

entries.notes: Europe's most famous songbird; at 200 tunes a minute it is the reason inns kept cages and poets kept silence.

entries.name: Common blackcap
entries.migrates: partial: many winter locally; British birds increasingly winter in Mediterranean gardens
behaviour: males black-capped, females rust-capped
rich warble from dense scrub; shy but unmistakable
feeds on garden scraps in winter in Mediterranean towns

voxel_model.pattern: grey-olive back, pale belly; black cap (male) or chestnut cap (female)

entries.notes: The garden warbler; increasingly wintering in Mediterranean villages on feeder tables, an accidental guest.

entries.name: European serin
entries.migrates: partial: flocks may wander altitudinally in winter
behaviour: tiny greenish-gold finch with a shivering trill
nests in conifers and fruit trees, sometimes in town parks
feeds on ripe and fallen weed seeds

voxel_model.pattern: yellow-green streaked brown, yellow rump and wing-bars

entries.notes: The spritely green-yellow chat of orchards; ancestor of the domestic canary's song culture.

entries.name: European goldfinch
entries.migrates: nomadic in winter: follows thistle crop
behaviour: red face, gold wing bar, black-and-white head: unmistakable
feeds daintily on thistle heads with tweezers bill
flocks straggle across fallow land in autumn

voxel_model.pattern: crimson face, tricolour black-white-red head, broad yellow wing bar

entries.notes: The milk of painters; trapped for cages since the Renaissance, but protected across the Mediterranean now.

entries.name: Common quail
entries.migrates: trans-Saharan migrant: autumn fall over Mediterranean coasts is biblical
behaviour: squat ground bird with whistled 'wet-my-lips' call at dusk
flushes reluctantly, rocketing out of grass
the quail of Exodus; autumn migrations fell exhausted on Mediterranean ships

voxel_model.pattern: mottled round plump body, striped head, pale eyebrow stripe

entries.notes: The only migratory game bird of Europe; pursued by every Mediterranean culture since the pharaohs.

entries.name: Barn owl
behaviour: ghost over the stubble fields: white heart-shaped face, no hoot, a rasping scream
nests in barn beams, dovecotes, churches and ruins
swallows prey whole; casts pellets of fur and bone

voxel_model.pattern: white face and belly, golden-buff mottled back

entries.notes: The ghost of the barn beam; farmers' ally against rats, haunted in every folklore as the death-bird.

entries.name: Little owl
behaviour: Athena's owl: white brow, flat walking gait, bobs and bows
day-active when hunting rodents; perches upright on fence posts and ruins
nests in olive-tree holes, walls and abandoned lanes

voxel_model.pattern: spotted grey-brown, bold white brow and throat

entries.notes: The coin-owl of Athens; still sits on telegraph poles over olive groves, flouting the sun with a flat stare.

entries.name: Eurasian scops owl
entries.migrates: winters in sub-Saharan Africa; summer visitor
behaviour: a single repetitive hollow whistle at dusk: 'tyu...tyu...tyu'
mimics dry leaves perfectly; camouflage in the cypress
hunts big insects close to trees, rarely far from cover

voxel_model.pattern: bark-streaked grey-brown, long ear tufts, pale eyebrows

entries.notes: The cicada's nocturnal shadow; you hear scops owl before you ever see it, and often hear only it.

entries.name: Common swift
entries.migrates: winters in southern Africa; returns with the first hot afternoons
behaviour: screaming parties over rooftops on warm evenings
may stay airborne for ten months without landing: sleeps on the wing
glues a saliva-nest to cliff or eave; never perches on a branch

voxel_model.pattern: sooty black with a pale throat; boomerang silhouette

entries.notes: The bird of the tower eave; towns time their summer to its scream, ten months of it spent entirely in the sky.

entries.name: Barn swallow
entries.migrates: winters in sub-Saharan Africa; returns March-April
behaviour: deep steel-blue back, cream belly, long tail streamers
nests glued with mud pellets under eaves and bridges
skims over fields and water hawking insects at low speed

voxel_model.pattern: glossy blue back and cap, rusty forehead and breast band, cream belly

entries.notes: The herald of the Mediterranean year; where the swallow nests, the spring is accounted for.

entries.name: Red-billed chough
entries.migrates: move between sea cliffs and high pastures with the seasons
behaviour: aerial acrobat: flips, glides and play-somersaults off sea cliffs
red bill and red legs against glossy black plumage
flocks rummage grazed turf for ants; increasing in coastal resorts

voxel_model.pattern: glossy black with a scarlet decurved bill and scarlet legs

entries.notes: The clown of the sea cliff; on Gibraltar, the Rock's self-appointed aerobatic display team.

entries.name: Italian wall lizard
behaviour: dozens bolt over sunlit terraces and stone walls
drops its tail when grabbed; regenerates a stubbier one
introduced far beyond Italy: Istanbul, Anatolian coast, Mediterranean islands

voxel_model.pattern: green to brown with a pale dorso-lateral stripe; males blue on flanks

entries.notes: The Italian terrace's wallpaper; a lizard you will meet every hundred metres in sunny brick.

entries.name: Moorish gecko
behaviour: clatters over sun-hot walls and indoor lamps at dusk
adhesive toe pads let it walk upside down on glass and plaster
vocal: clicking and squeaking while hunting

voxel_model.pattern: grey with warty tubercles in rows, pale around the eyes

entries.notes: The moth's shadow that walks up walls; a permanent tenant of whitewashed Mediterranean houses.

entries.name: Ladder snake
behaviour: juveniles show a bold ladder of dark bars along the spine; adults are plain olive
constricts rodents; basks in stone walls then hunts barns at dusk
displays with flattened S-pose and hisses, but is reluctant to bite

voxel_model.pattern: olive-brown; juveniles barred like a ladder-back chair

entries.notes: The barn's quiet custodian in the Iberian dehesa; mistaken for vipers by the frightened, and wrongly killed for it.

entries.name: European glass lizard
behaviour: legless but a lizard, not a snake: movable eyelids and ear openings
breaks its own tail into glassy segments when seized
hunts rodents and beetles in rocky steppe and vineyards

voxel_model.pattern: shiny olive-brown, darker head and dorsal stripe in juveniles

entries.notes: The eastern Mediterranean's metre-long legless phantom; in Greek folklore it is an eyeless dragon of the hills.

entries.name: Iberian ribbed newt
behaviour: ribs poke through the flanks as a defence when its sides arch upward
regenerates legs, tail, spinal cord and even parts of its brain
a major laboratory model for limb regeneration research

voxel_model.pattern: chocolate brown with orange rib-tips along the sides

entries.notes: The cork-ribbed water dragon of Iberian ponds; in defensive pose its ribs exit its skin like tiny spears.

entries.name: Parsley frog
behaviour: green flecks scattered like chopped parsley over a grey-brown back
tadpoles hatch in late winter pools and can remain tadpoles all summer
metamorphoses are explosive and synchronised after rain

voxel_model.pattern: dark grey-brown marbled with vivid green parsley-speckles

entries.notes: The frog you wear as parsley; the western Mediterranean's rain-frog, appearing for one loud week a year.

entries.name: Large-clawed scorpion
behaviour: Europe's largest scorpion; hides under stones by day, hunts by night
glows vivid cyan under UV torchlight
European sting is painful but mild; North African tunetanus subspecies can be serious

voxel_model.pattern: yellow to yellow-brown, thin-fingered pincers, striped tail

entries.notes: The Mediterranean's only genuinely feared scorpion; in alpine Spain it endures snow, which surprises everyone.

entries.name: Mediterranean wolf spider
behaviour: the original tarantula: Taranto, Puglia, Italy
digs a silk-lined burrow in soft ground and ambushes at the mouth
carries its egg sac behind it like luggage; spiderlings ride on her back

voxel_model.pattern: dark brown hairy body with two pale stripes on the cephalothorax

entries.notes: Bitten dancers of the 1500s were cured by frenzied tarantella dancing; the spider's bite is actually innocuous.

entries.name: Painted lady
entries.migrates: trans-Mediterranean mass migrant: billions cross from Africa to Europe each spring
behaviour: the great butterfly of antiquity; Aristotle and Roman writers recorded its mass migrations
larvae eat thistles and mallows; adults sip nectar and rotting fruit
in swarm years, clouds of orange butterflies cross the coasts in May

voxel_model.pattern: orange-black-white marbled forewings, eyespots on hindwings

entries.notes: The butterfly of the Exodus route; in May, Spanish skies can fill with orange.

entries.name: Italian tree cicada
behaviour: males sing at 80-90 dB from treetops on the hottest afternoons
larva lives 2 to 4 years underground, sucking root xylem, then erupts
empty shells split down the back cling to bark by the thousands

voxel_model.pattern: brown-grey with reddish abdomen segments; wings with dark vein marks

entries.notes: The metronome of Mediterranean noon; the sound of an Italian July, louder than conversation.

entries.name: Spanish fly
behaviour: metallic gold-green blister beetle; reflex bleeds from leg joints when handled
larvae are parasitoids of solitary bee nests, eating the bee stores
source of cantharidin: ancient aphrodisiac, toxic in doses

voxel_model.pattern: brilliant metallic green-gold carapace

entries.notes: The apothecary's famous aphrodisiac; in reality blistering, vomiting and a kidney emergency.

entries.name: Great capricorn beetle
behaviour: huge longhorn whose larvae spend 3-4 years boring into living ancient oaks
males fly on hot June evenings, scenting females from oak to oak
strictly protected in the EU; a flag of old wood pasture

voxel_model.pattern: black body, reddish-brown tips to the wing cases; males carry antennae longer than the body

entries.notes: The old oak's shining knight; if it lives here, the oak pasture is three thousand years in the making.

entries.name: Western honey bee
entries.migrates: swarms abscond; drones abandoned to famine in winter
behaviour: managed hives yield honey, wax and pollination; wild hives nest in tree hollows and wall voids
Mediterranean subspecies: ligustica (Italy), iberiensis (Iberia), cecropia (Greece)
waggle dance tells the swarm the direction and distance of flowers

voxel_model.pattern: golden fuzz, black stripes, orange-amber eyes

entries.notes: The thread that binds every Mediterranean orchard; an oracle, an army, and a jar of gold.

entries.name: Common glow-worm
behaviour: wingless females climb stalks to glow green-yellow through June and July
males fly to the brightest female; light seen up to 45 m
larvae stalk snails for 2-3 years, injecting them with digestive enzymes

voxel_model.pattern: black female body with three glowing segments; males smaller, winged, brown

entries.notes: The living night-light of old meadows; light pollution is now its main enemy across Europe.

entries.name: Mediterranean harvester ant
behaviour: colonies of huge granaries under stone nests in dry fields
marches in lines kilometres long to carry whole seeds home
queen may live 20 years; the nest outlives the farmer

voxel_model.pattern: black with a glossy reddish head and thorax; large soldier heads

entries.notes: The granary keeper of the dry Mediterranean; its seed roads are older than the estate's hedges.

entries.name: Garden snail
behaviour: sealed inside a dried mucus epiphragm during summer drought
herb of Mediterranean gardens; both escargot and pest
leaves cream-and-brown swirled shells on old walls after every rain

voxel_model.pattern: chestnut-and-cream swirled shell with darker flecks

entries.notes: L'escargot; a French delicacy whose shells grace every Mediterranean wall after rain.

entries.name: Sand smelt
behaviour: clouds of silver-green dart through shallow lagoons and estuaries
schools shimmer in brackish harbours across the whole Mediterranean
sold fried whole as pescaditos in Spain and cieche in Venice

voxel_model.pattern: translucent silver with a bright lateral stripe; green back

entries.notes: The flickering silver of every estuary; fried whole, it is the Mediterranean's answer to whitebait.
